passage: One morning in a small apartment in Bombay, a girl of about sixteen looked up from the newspaper she was reading and said excitedly, “Pandit Ravi Shankar is playing tomorrow at the Shanmukhananda Auditorium!” “Sh-sh,” said her mother, pointing to the boy lying on the bed. “You’ll wake him up. subject: English

ans: Columbus embarked on his voyage with a strong will to discover a new world for his King and Queen. subject: English

q: Why were the people of Tibet unhappy? (Give an account of the difficulties experienced by the people of Tibet.)
ans: The people of Tibet were very poor and miserable. Their land had no rivers, no fertile soil, no warmth, and no fresh flowers. They suffered constantly from extreme cold and hunger all year round.

subject: English
q: What did the old folk of Tibet say about happiness?
ans: The old folk said that happiness was a beautiful bird that lived on a high snowy mountain far away in the East, and wherever the bird flew, happiness followed it.

subject: English
q: Who was selected to find the Bird of Happiness? What was done on his departure?
ans: A bright and brave boy named Wangjia was selected. On his departure, the village girls offered him barley wine and the mothers sprinkled barley grains on his head to wish him a safe journey.

subject: English
q: What did the first monster ask Wangjia to do? How did Wangjia react to it?
ans: The first monster ordered Wangjia to kill Lousang's mother if he wanted to see the Bird of Happiness. Wangjia refused, saying that he loved his own mother and would never kill someone else's mother.

subject: English
q: How did the first old monster punish Wangjia? Why did Wangjia feel "Will I ever make it?"?
ans: The monster blew on his long beard and turned the smooth road into a vast scree of knife-sharp stones. Wangjia's boots tore, his feet and hands were cut to shreds, causing him such excruciating pain that he doubted if he would survive.

subject: English
q: How did Wangjia react to the second monster?
ans: The second monster asked Wangjia to poison old gaffer Sillong. Wangjia flatly refused, stating that he loved his own grandfather and would never kill another person's grandfather.

subject: English
q: How did the second monster make Wangjia suffer?
ans: The monster blew through his beard, blowing away Wangjia's bread bag and turning the fertile land into a boundless desert with no food. Wangjia suffered from intense hunger, dizziness, and sharp stomach pain.

subject: English
q: What did the third monster warn Wangjia? How did Wangjia respond?
ans: The third monster warned Wangjia to bring girl Bhima's eyeballs or have his own gouged out. Wangjia bravely responded that nobody had the right to destroy the eyes of an innocent, pretty girl.

subject: English
q: How was the third journey difficult for Wangjia?
ans: When Wangjia refused the evil deed, the third monster gouged out his eyeballs, leaving him completely blind. He had to painfully grope and crawl on his hands and knees for nine hundred miles.

subject: English
q: What contrast do you draw between the wishes of the monsters and the wish of Wangjia?
ans: The three monsters had cruel and destructive wishes that aimed to harm and murder innocent human beings, whereas Wangjia's only wish was selfless: to bring prosperity, joy, and happiness to his suffering villagers.

subject: English
q: What do you like the most in the story 'The Bird of Happiness'? Support your answer with reasons.
ans: I admire Wangjia's unshakeable courage, patience, and moral integrity. Even when threatened with torture, starvation, and blindness, he never chose the easy way of harming others, remaining dedicated to his people.

subject: English
q: What hardships did Wangjia undergo on his way to find the bird?

subject: English
q: How did the Bird of Happiness put an end to the hardships suffered by the people with its three cries?

subject: English
q: What changes came over Wangjia as the Bird of Happiness caressed him?
ans: His eyeballs flew back into their sockets giving him brighter vision than before, all his painful wounds were healed, he became stronger than ever, and he was offered dried meat and cream cakes.

subject: English
q: How can you say that Wangjia was a brave boy?
ans: Wangjia was brave because he fearlessly faced three terrifying monsters, refused their evil demands without flinching, endured terrible physical torture, and persevered to the mountain summit to save his village.

subject: English
q: In what way was the Bird of Happiness guarded?
ans: The Bird of Happiness was fiercely guarded by three old monsters with deadly powers who could kill a person simply by blowing through their long beards.

subject: English

ans: The villagers knew that the journey was extremely long, dangerous, and guarded by deadly monsters. They offered him barley wine, grains, and provisions to show their gratitude and pray for his safe return.

subject: English
q: Why did Wangjia decide not to go back from his journey?
ans: Whenever Wangjia felt weak and overwhelmed by pain, he remembered that the suffering people of his village were eagerly waiting for him to bring back happiness. This inspired him to keep moving forward.

subject: English

ans: Wangjia walked toward the East for many days because the Tibetan elders had told him that the Bird of Happiness lived on a high snowy mountain located in the East.
